For the NASA Space Apps Challenge, I want to build health monitoring software for astronauts using AI and data analysis to detect unusual patterns and display insights on a dashboard. summary:
AstroCare is an autonomous biomedical monitoring and clinical decision-support platform engineered to safeguard astronaut health during deep-space exploration missions (e.g., Artemis and Mars). 

To address the communication latency of deep space, AstroCare operates an on-board, unsupervised Machine Learning engine utilizing Multivariate Isolation Forest (100 decision trees) to detect multivariate physiological anomalies in real time across cardiac, respiratory, thermoregulatory, and dosimetric telemetry. 

The system directly addresses the five NASA Human Spaceflight Hazards by correlating biometric excursions against 12 official NASA Human Research Program (HRP) risk modules. AstroCare delivers actionable, tiered countermeasure protocols—spanning immediate astronaut interventions, preventive habitat adjustments, and flight surgeon triage notes—with verified NASA/CSA scientific citations. 

By enabling autonomous, offline-first health surveillance without relying on real-time Earth communication, AstroCare ensures early clinical intervention and mission resilience on the lunar surface and beyond.
details:
AstroCare is an autonomous, on-board astronaut biomedical monitoring and clinical decision-support platform designed for deep-space exploration missions such as Artemis and future crewed Mars expeditions.

How it works:

AstroCare streams multidimensional physiological telemetry—including heart rate, SpO2, blood pressure, core body temperature, respiration rate, sleep duration, and radiation exposure. It runs an on-board, unsupervised Multivariate Isolation Forest machine learning algorithm (100 decision trees) to evaluate complex correlations across all vitals simultaneously. When statistical deviations occur, the system automatically correlates them with NASA's five Human Spaceflight Hazards and generates evidence-based, tiered countermeasure protocols (Immediate Astronaut Actions, Preventive Habitat Adjustments, and Flight Surgeon Console Triage).

Benefits and Impact:

1. Zero Latency Dependency: Solves the 5- to 22-minute communication delay between Mars and Earth by enabling autonomous, offline-first health surveillance directly on the spacecraft.

2. Multivariate Early Warning: Catches subtle, combined physiological shifts that standard single-parameter threshold alarms miss, such as microgravity cephalad fluid redistribution, exercise-induced thermal storage impairment, and cumulative radiation surges.

3. Reduced Cognitive Fatigue: Translates raw data into plain-language clinical insights, color-coded severity tiers, and clear countermeasure checklists to support astronauts during high-stress EVA intervals.

Tools, Languages, and Software Used:

- Languages: TypeScript, JavaScript (Node.js runtime), Python (scikit-learn prototype), SQL, HTML5, CSS3.

- Frontend Framework: React 18, Vite build tool, Recharts for dynamic telemetry visualizations, and Lucide-react.

- Backend & Storage: Node.js REST API service with an embedded SQLite datastore.

- Cloud Hosting & CI/CD: Render (Static Site & Node Web Service) and GitHub.

Creativity and Factors Considered:

AstroCare bridges advanced unsupervised machine learning with the official 12 NASA Human Research Program (HRP) Risk Modules. Instead of simply flagging an alert, it provides actionable, peer-reviewed clinical countermeasures and scientific citations. The interface was engineered specifically for extreme environments: high-contrast dark mode to preserve dark adaptation, fast sub-second responsiveness, and complete mobile and tablet adaptability for astronaut wearable and handheld displays.
